correctness.rationale: PASS: The associated evaluation weight is exactly v_alpha, since analytic boundary peaks (1-conj(eta)w)^(-alpha) attain (1-r)^(-alpha) and obey the norm bound; Bonet 2022 Theorem 53 supplies the single-symbol essential norm m^(-alpha), and Calkin triangle inequality gives the upper bound. For the lower bound, read all factors of the explicit package peaks u_(j,n), with near-boundary exponent eps=sqrt(1-r)>0 and angular high power floor((1-r)^(-1/2)). Each u belongs to the little growth space (vanishing weighted modulus at every boundary point), satisfies norm<=2^eps and diagonal weighted value ->1 at r^(m_j) eta_j. Pick boundary eta_j=zeta^(m_j) pairwise distinct, so off-diagonal terms vanish uniformly and aligned phase summation has norm ->1. Weighted embeddings into C_0 and dominated convergence against any finite measure show this bounded locally-null sequence is weakly null; compact perturbations vanish. Directly checked asymptotic diagonal limits for alpha=1/2,1,3/2 and m=1,2,3,7; proof, not finite numeric tests, establishes every alpha, N. No repeated symbols, infinite sums or other weights claimed.

value.rationale: PASS: Essential norms classify distance to compactness and asymptotic operator size. Finite linear combinations need not attain the triangle upper bound because cancellation is possible, so exact additivity for a natural family of boundary-separating monomial symbols provides a useful complete formula, stronger than per-symbol norms. The value lies in the separation mechanism and exact noncancellation, not in a routine three-term numerical example.
